blocks.text: What Appliances Do We Remove in Toronto?

c: We handle all household and
commercial appliances
— big or small, working or broken. Here’s a breakdown of what we take:

Fridges are bulky, awkward, and surprisingly heavy. Whether it’s a standard unit or a side-by-side double door, our Toronto team gets it out safely — even from tight basements and narrow hallways. Working units get donated locally when possible.
Front-loaders, top-loaders, stackable units, standalone dryers — we remove all of them across Toronto homes and apartments. Laundry rooms are one of our most common jobs.
Gas or electric, freestanding or built-in — we disconnect and haul away stoves and ovens. We follow proper safety protocols for gas appliances before any removal begins.
Built-in or countertop, we remove both. Dishwasher removal often involves some plumbing disconnection, which our team handles as part of the job.
Tank water heaters, air conditioners, and dehumidifiers all qualify. These are heavy items that most people can’t safely move alone — our crew is equipped for exactly this.
Clearing a rental property, renovating a kitchen, or managing a multi-unit building? We do bulk appliance removal across Toronto at better rates. This is also a great time to combine with our

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions — Appliance Removal Toronto

items.q: Q: How do I get rid of old appliances in Toronto?
a: A: The easiest option by far is calling a local appliance removal company like Live Junk Free. You book a time, we show up, we carry everything out, and we handle disposal — recycling and donation where possible. If your appliance still works, you could list it on Kijiji or Facebook Marketplace. The City of Toronto also has a large item pickup program for certain appliances — check toronto.ca for scheduled pickup dates in your area. That said, if you need it gone quickly or the appliance is broken, professional removal is the most practical route.

items.q: Q: What is the easiest way to dispose of appliances?
a: A: Hiring a professional removal team is genuinely the easiest way — you don’t move anything yourself, you don’t need to figure out where it goes, and it’s done in under an hour in most cases. For free disposal, the City of Toronto’s large item collection program accepts certain appliances at scheduled times. Some appliance retailers also offer haul-away of your old unit when they deliver a new one — worth asking when you make your purchase. For broken or unusable appliances, a junk removal service like ours is your simplest path forward.

items.q: Q: Does the City of Toronto offer free appliance removal?
a: A: Yes, the City of Toronto has a large item collection program that includes certain appliances. You can schedule through toronto.ca — typically requiring a few days’ notice. Keep in mind you’d need to bring the appliance to the curb yourself, and not all appliance types are accepted. For anything urgent, in a tight space, or not covered by the city program, a private removal service is faster and far more convenient.

items.q: Q: Can you remove appliances from a condo or apartment in Toronto?
a: A: Absolutely — condo and apartment appliance removal is something we do across Toronto regularly. We coordinate elevator access where needed, follow building rules, and use the right equipment for narrow hallways and tight stairwells. Just mention the building details when you book and we’ll plan accordingly.

items.q: Q: Do you recycle appliances in Toronto?
a: A: Yes. Working appliances go to local Toronto donation programs or charity resellers where possible. For broken units, we sort the materials — metals, plastics, refrigerants — and take them to certified recycling facilities. We actively try to keep as much as possible out of landfill. Eco-friendly appliance removal in Toronto is something we genuinely practise, not just market speak.
